utterances.text: Mr. Radic, the last comment you made concerning Naser Oric and Kemo, is it true that you have been telling the Trial Chamber the absolute truth to the best your recollection in terms of the person purportedly called Naser Oric?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I would like to ask the Trial Chamber if we could make two small corrections to the record.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Mr. Radic, on two occasions, and I can point specifically at the points of the transcript where you mentioned October 25th as the day before you were released, were you referring to the 15th of October and not the 25th of October, 1992?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the 16th of October when we were exchanged, not the 26th or the 25th.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And day before you were exchanged is the 15th October 1992? Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Very briefly, Mr. Radic, could you please tell the Trial Chamber if at any times during your stay at the prison whether you or any of the other inmates had cigarette burns placed on parts of their body.

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not. I don't know about the others.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: When you were at times hit with the blows of the pieces of wood, would you raise your hand in order to attempt to stop such blows?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Were there times that your lands hit instead of having your body hit because you were successfully able to stop the blows that were coming at you?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I would like to go to Sanction very briefly and show a part of the videotape, the part that shows Mr. Sarac. I believe that's Prosecution Exhibit 98.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: We have transcript. I don't see sound for the purpose of Mr. Radic. I'd like to know, could we have sound on that part. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Mr. Radic, is it possible that Mr. Sarac did have cigarette burns on his hand as a result of having stayed in the prison?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether they extinguished cigarettes on his hand. The marks on his hands were from cleaning the toilet, I think. As for cigarettes, I'm not sure. If they did extinguish cigarettes on him, they did it when I was not around.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Mr. Radic, isn't it true that when you went in to be interrogated, you mentioned that there was someone who was a Croat in addition to the chief of police, Mr. Mrki Mirzet, that during that interrogation you've testified that you were kicked in the face and it caused bleeding at least in the room, the interrogation room?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, I would like to -- the name I referred to Mrki, or Mirzet, it might be a mispronunciation on my part, I'm sure the Trial Chamber understands. I would like you to look at this next part of the videotape again, and I hope that the sound is up, Your Honours, for this portion.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Radic, you testified earlier that you were not in the room where Mr. Sarac was being interrogated by the man from Croatia and from the chief of police. But isn't it possible that he too was hit in the face --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Asking him to speculate. If he wasn't there, he doesn't know. Simple as that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That would be pure speculation.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Let me rephrase that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Mr. Radic, do you remember when Mr. Sarac came from the interrogation, having been interrogated by the man from Croatia and the police of chief [sic] that he too had marks on his face or possibly on his head, as described in this video?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I think he had a bruise on his face, and he was holding tight onto his head, the top of his head. I don't -- didn't notice anything else. I wasn't there. I didn't see what went on in there.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Radic, another part of the video there was mention of some sexual violence, and Mr. Sarac states, and this is on page 3 of the transcript: "They beat you --" and he replies something like electricity --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I didn't cross-examine on this. I don't see how this arises from cross-examination. It may be something the Prosecution has thought of subsequently but if they're going to raise it, I will have to re-cross-examine on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's a valid point.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You did ask --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Nothing about electricity, though.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, but the witness did mention that he doesn't agree with what Sarac said because, according to him, there was no electricity but that was in reply to one of your questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: That was in examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: That was in examination-in-chief, but Counsellor did bring up whether Mr. Sarac had on several occasions, and Mr. Radic noted that he might not have been forthcoming and truthful on the tape, and I'm leading back into an area might have been -- Counsellor might have been referring to as being untruthful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But it wasn't an area that counsel referred to as regarding Sarac being untruthful, it was the witness himself.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: This is true on direct, but on cross-examination counsel tried to have the witness state that Mr. Sarac might have been untruthful at parts in the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It was at a different point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Which the witness didn't agree with because he said it could be one way or it could be the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: He's also going to be asked to speculate about this matter because he doesn't have any personal knowledge --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I'll withdraw the question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- arises out of the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I'll withdraw the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Mr. Radic, you were interviewed by the Office of the Prosecutor, and that has now become Defence Exhibit 161. That was an interview that we've established took place in May of 2000, May 25th. Now, during that interview, you've testified -- I'm sorry. You stated that Mr. Naser Oric began kicking and beating Sarac, and that's in reference to the third time you saw Mr. Oric. Do you remember that part of the interview? You'll have to say yes for the record.

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And you testified that it appeared that the person purporting to be Naser Oric slid his -- slid his leg up -- I'll just try and get the quote. "Slid his leg up the man's body," referring to Sarac. Could you please explain to the Trial Chamber, after the man purporting to be Naser Oric slid his leg up the man's body purported to be Mr. Sarac, was Mr. Sarac injured or not injured from this contact between the man purportedly Mr. Oric and the leg of Mr. Sarac? Were there injuries that ensued?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there was an injury to his face. I believe I said so today and before. He hit him once. And I believe later he sort of put his leg up against him, and Sarac fell against his leg and he was hurting, I don't know from what.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: When Mr. Sarac fell against his leg, and I imagine meaning the leg of the person referred to as Naser Oric, did it appear that Mr. Sarac was injured or hurt from having fell against his leg?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he had no visible injuries, but he must have been injured since he fell on the floor, and he probably felt pain in his leg.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: The witness said yesterday that Sarac didn't fall at all. I might have to re-cross examine on this.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe the witness said yesterday that after he was hit he remained standing. Now we're talking about a second contact that I believe came up with cross-examination and that concerned the contact with the leg, and I just wanted to clarify that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Go ahead and let's bring it to an end, Ms. Sellers, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I will just go to my last three sets of questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: In the interview that you gave to the Office of the Prosecutor, you stated that you answered questions that were asked of you; isn't that correct? And did you try and answer those questions as thoroughly as possible, those that were asked to you?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Were you --

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Were you asked at that interview to give a description of the person that we have referred to today as Naser Oric?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I would like to read to you from page 7 of Defence Exhibit D161, and it concerns a description of the person purported to be Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I asked the witness to confirm that description yesterday and he did. So I don't know if -- we can probably skip that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This precisely entitles the Prosecution to re-examine --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I mean, he's being asked the same question again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't know what the question is. She hasn't -- she hasn't put the question as yet.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Mr. Radic, did you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If it's the same question, I will stop.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Mr. Radic, did you inform the Office of the Prosecutor the following: "I will describe him for you. Naser Oric had a strong build. He was not tall, maybe 160 centimetres. He had dark brown hair and was clean-shaven. I think Naser Oric had blue eyes. He was quite young. I don't think he was even 30 years old at the time, which was in 1992. He was dressed in a yellow khaki beige-green camouflage uniform which is called an American uniform. On the left breast pocket of his shirt he wore a patch and -- that had lilies on it. It was a special uniform. Only he and Mrki, FNU or LNU, wore uniforms like that. Later I met another commander named Mrki, FNU or LNU. Naser Oric also carried a pistol on his right hip." Is this the type of character detail -- characteristics, physical and dressing, that you gave the Office of the Prosecutor during that interview?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, from what I saw, and I confirm that statement. I'm only slightly confused about the hair. He had a short haircut, but for the most part I can confirm that description. It tallies with my later sightings of Mr. Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And Your Honour, my last two questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Mr. Radic, during that same interview, on page 11 of that interview, were you asked whether you would be able to recognise Naser Oric again, the person purported to be Naser Oric? Do you remember whether you were asked whether you would recognise the person purported to be Naser Oric again? And isn't it true that you told the interviewer that I will --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's take them one by one first because he hasn't confirmed --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, he nodded to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Could you please say yes or no for the record because of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And didn't you tell the Office of the Prosecutor at that time, "I will be able to recognise Naser Oric, Zulfo Tursunovic, Kemo Ahmetovic, Mrki first name or last name unknown, and Cude, if I ever saw them again." Wasn't that what you told the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Judge Brydensholt, I take it you don't have questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BRYDENSHOLT
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Judge Eser.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: I will limit myself to one question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Mr. Radic, have you ever been told why you have been captured or why you have been kept in the prison? Was there ever given any reason for this?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. I knew the reason I was captured and I was kept there, but nobody came to tell us why we were there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: And while you were being beaten, did these people talk to you or did they do it silently, without saying anything?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There were insults, slurs directed at us. They told us, "Chetniks, you are firing at our children, throwing grenades," and then the beatings followed. They wanted us to admit to being Chetniks, which I didn't do because I wasn't one in the first place, and secondly, it was an insult. I thought "Chetnik" and "Ustasha" were equally bad.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: So is it correct to conclude that you never have been told that you might be exchanged?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I said that Hrustic also came to see us once at the cell before he was killed. I believe it's in one of my statements. He told us we would be exchanged, and we would be treated according to the Geneva Conventions. I believe it is somewhere in my statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Radic, that brings your testimony to an end. I thought it would last less, but it didn't. But at least we're finished. So you're free to go, go back to your country. On behalf of the Trial Chamber and on behalf of Judge Brydensholt and behalf of Judge Eser, I'd like to thank you for having come over to give testimony. You will be assisted by members of my staff, and we'll do our best to facilitate your return back home as soon as possible. Once more, I thank you, and I wish you a safe journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, too, Your Honours. I also wish to thank everybody else in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do I have the indulgence of everyone? We know that we have overstepped by at least five minutes, but I would like, out of courtesy, to say a few words to the witness so that I apologise to him and explain to him why we haven't started with his testimony. It will only last a couple of minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: It's okay with the interpreters, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. And his name is ...

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, his name is Branimir Mitrovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you think we will finish with him tomorrow, this witness? No, I suppose not. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I thought I'd probably be quite short with him, not more than an hour and a half.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Mitrovic, good afternoon to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's a good feeling to see you smiling, because for a moment I thought you would be a little bit angry with us because we've kept you waiting here for hours without starting with your testimony. I do feel -- I do feel sorry for that, and I do apologise to you. However, I would like you to know that this was not capricious. What happened is that the previous witness, with whom we should have finished last week, we didn't finish with him last week. We continued today, and we were hoping to finish with him after about two or three hours, not more than that, but unfortunately we couldn't finish with his testimony until a couple of minutes ago. So please do accept my apologies and those of the Tribunal. We will be starting with your testimony straight away first thing tomorrow morning at 9.00, and we will do our level best this time to try and see -- make sure that you go back home as quickly as you can, maybe a little bit earlier than anticipated. Once more, I thank you for being patient and for your understanding, and you will be escorted and given all the attention that -- and assistance you require and then we'll meet tomorrow morning at 9.00. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So that's it. I think we can adjourn, and once more I should like to thank all the staff, the technicians, the interpreters, and the courtroom staff, plus of course counsel, Prosecution and parties, for your indulgence and we'll meet tomorrow morning at 9.00. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
